title: Incident-driven observability catchup: dashboards, traces, and SLO instrumentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity-stress event on 2026-02-24 we observed sustained request queues and elevated 99th percentile latency for a subset of hosted model routes. The incident response revealed multiple observability blind spots that slowed diagnosis and prolonged mitigation: missing per-model inflight-queue metrics, dashboards that only showed aggregate p50/p95 and hid tail regressions, absence of tracing spans for runtime kernel-selection and KV-cache hit/miss, and no firing alert tuned to cross-model 99th percentile latency regressions.

Goal: Close the gaps so that next capacity/regression incident can be diagnosed in <30m and remediated without broad throttles. Deliverables: new metrics, new dashboards/views in Console, runtime tracing spans, alert rule updates, and a post-deploy validation runbook.

Observed blind spots: 
- No single metric for per-model request queue length (existing queue-length metric aggregated cluster-wide).
- Latency dashboard aggregates across all models and routes; a narrow, high-tail regression for named routes was invisible.
- Traces stop at the request deserialization layer; kernel selection, quantization path, and KV cache outcomes are not emitting spans.
- No histogram-based 99th/99.9th percentile alert; existing alerts are based on p95 only.
- Dashboards lacked quick links to correlated infra signals (GPU util by node-pool, evictions, and model instance restarts).

Action items (owner + ETA):
1) Add per-model/request-route inflight queue metric emitted by serving runtime (owner: Jonah Kim) — ETA 2026-03-05.
2) Add boolean KV cache hit/miss spans and a short-lived metric for cache-hit-rate by model (owner: Priya Shah) — ETA 2026-03-08.
3) Create a set of per-model latency dashboards (p50/p95/p99/p999 + request rate + queue length) and an aggregate page that surfaces models with worst p99 delta (owner: Observability UX, reviewer: Lina Moreno) — ETA 2026-03-12.
4) Add runtime trace spans for kernel selection decisions and quantization fallback path, with tags for model-version and sequence-length bucket (owner: Runtime team, assignee: Marco Ruiz) — ETA 2026-03-10.
5) Introduce a firing alert: model-route p99 latency > baseline + 250ms sustained 5m OR p999 > baseline + 500ms (owner: SRE, assignee: Hana Liu) — ETA 2026-03-09.
6) Add dashboard quick-links to node-pool GPU utilization and eviction counts, and include a one-click drilldown to affected instances (owner: Console infra) — ETA 2026-03-12.
7) Post-deploy verification runbook + playbook snippet for on-call to triage queue vs kernel problems (owner: SRE) — ETA 2026-03-15.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Per-model queue metric emitted for 95% of production model routes and visible in Console.
- New per-model dashboards show p50/p95/p99/p999 and queue length; p99-based alert fires in the staging canary during a synthetic tail test.
- Trace spans for kernel selection and KV cache presence available in distributed tracing with searchable tags.
- Runbook validated by SRE during a tabletop drill and linked from Console incident page.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Emitting per-model queue metrics increases cardinality; to mitigate, we'll emit for top 200 routes by traffic and aggregate others into "other_routes" bucket. We evaluated full cardinality (too expensive) vs sampling (loses fidelity) and chose bounded-top-k.
- Tracing every kernel-selection path adds overhead; spans will be emitted at DEBUG-level by default and elevated for routes with active alerts. We will enable lightweight sampling for traces by default to keep overhead <2%.

Rollout plan: implement metrics + dashboards in staging -> run synthetic tail-load test (script: infra/tests/latency-tail-test) -> validate alert fires -> promote to canary cluster -> enable in prod.

Links & artifacts: postmortem doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/2026-02-24+-+Capacity+event+postmortem, incident timeline: https://incident.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0224-01, initial investigation notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/observability-investigation, synthetic test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/pull/214
